title: Marketing Maverick
theme: Launch & market a new product in a competitive Indian market
description: You've got a brilliant product idea and a limited budget. Can you outsmart your competitors, win customers, and build a brand that stands out? Use marketing strategy, creativity, and data-driven decisions to dominate the market!
learning_objectives: Understand core marketing concepts (4Ps, segmentation, positioning)
Learn to allocate budgets strategically across marketing channels
Practice data-driven decision making with customer feedback
Understand competitive strategy and market dynamics

ai_image_config.art_direction: Modern colorful illustration style, Indian teens in contemporary settings, warm vibrant colors, educational and inspiring mood

scenes.title: The Spark
scenes.narrative: You're sitting in your school's Innovation Club when the teacher announces a challenge: create a real product and sell it at the upcoming Inter-School Mela! You've been sketching ideas in your notebook for weeks. Now it's time to pick one and go all in.
scenes.image_prompt: Indian teenager sitting in a colorful modern school classroom with Innovation Club banner, sketching product ideas in a notebook, other students brainstorming in background, warm lighting, vibrant educational illustration

choices.label: I'll build a smart hydration bottle with tracking stickers — it's eco-friendly and tech-savvy
choices.description: A reusable bottle with a hydration tracking sticker system — eco-friendly and tech-savvy.

choices.label: I want to create a desi fusion snack box that mixes Indian flavours with global twists
choices.description: A subscription snack box mixing traditional Indian flavors with global twists.

choices.label: I think a curated study buddy kit with stationery and flashcards would be perfect for students
choices.description: A curated stationery + flashcard kit designed by students, for students.

scenes.title: Know Your Customer
scenes.narrative: Great choice! But before you spend a single rupee, you need to understand who would actually buy this. Your Innovation Club advisor, Professor Priya, reminds you: 'The best products solve real problems for real people.' Time for some market research!
scenes.image_prompt: Indian teen conducting market research, talking to diverse group of students in a school courtyard, holding a clipboard with survey questions, colorful and engaging educational illustration

choices.label: I'll create a quick Google Form and blast it on our school WhatsApp groups for fast feedback
choices.description: Create a quick Google Form and share it across school WhatsApp groups. Fast and free!

choices.label: I'd rather talk to 20 students personally — it takes longer but I'll get much deeper insights
choices.description: Talk to 20 students personally. Takes time but gives deep insights.

scenes.title: Launch Day Approaches!
scenes.narrative: Your research is done, your product is ready, and the Inter-School Mela is just two weeks away. You have ₹10,000 in your club budget, a team of 3 friends, and a fierce competitor — Sneha Kapoor from the neighboring school — who's launching her own product. Game on!
scenes.image_prompt: Excited Indian teenagers preparing for a school market fair, setting up a colorful product booth with banners and samples, competitive energy, bright and inspiring illustration

npcs.name: Professor Priya
npcs.personality: Wise, encouraging, uses real-world Indian brand examples (Amul, Flipkart, Nykaa). Asks Socratic questions rather than giving direct answers.
npcs.backstory: A former CMO of a top Indian D2C startup who now teaches marketing at the National Institute of Design. She loves mentoring young entrepreneurs and believes every student has an inner marketer.
npcs.system_prompt_addon: You specialize in marketing strategy for young Indian entrepreneurs. Reference Indian brands like Amul, Zomato, Nykaa, boAt, and Flipkart. Use Hindi words occasionally (like 'jugaad', 'dhandha'). Keep advice actionable and age-appropriate.

npcs.name: Arjun
npcs.personality: Honest, slightly picky, represents the average Indian teen buyer. Gives candid product feedback.
npcs.backstory: A 15-year-old from Mumbai who carefully evaluates every purchase with his pocket money. He's active on Instagram, loves unboxing videos, and always checks reviews before buying.
npcs.system_prompt_addon: You are a typical Indian teen customer. Give honest, sometimes blunt feedback about products and marketing. Mention platforms like Instagram, YouTube, and WhatsApp. Talk about pocket money and value for money.

competitors.name: Sneha Kapoor
competitors.description: CEO of the rival school's Innovation Club. Well-funded, confident, and always one step ahead. But sometimes her aggressive tactics backfire.
competitors.chat_personality: Competitive and confident, occasionally taunting but always respectful. Uses marketing jargon to sound impressive. Deep down, she respects good strategy.

base_rounds.title: Round 1: Brand Identity
base_rounds.story: Your product needs a name, logo, and tagline. First impressions matter — especially at a crowded mela. Sneha has already hired a design student for her brand. What's your move?
base_rounds.image_prompt: Indian teenager brainstorming brand designs at a desk covered in colorful logo sketches, mood boards, and paint swatches, creative sparks flying, modern school art room setting, vibrant and imaginative illustration
base_rounds.goal: Create a compelling brand identity within your budget

choices.label: DIY with Canva
choices.description: Design your own brand materials using free tools. Save money but spend time.
choices.feedback: Your DIY brand has a raw, authentic feel! Customers appreciate the personal touch. You saved budget for later, and your Canva skills got a boost. Smart move for a bootstrapped marketer!

choices.label: Hire a Design Student
choices.description: Pay ₹2,000 to a senior design student for professional branding.
choices.feedback: Professional quality makes a difference! Your brand looks polished and trustworthy. The investment is significant for your budget, but in marketing, perception is everything.

choices.label: Run a Design Contest
choices.description: Ask schoolmates to submit designs for a ₹500 prize. Generates buzz!
choices.feedback: Brilliant marketing move! The contest itself became a marketing campaign. Students are talking about your brand even before launch. This is what marketers call 'earned media' — free publicity from word of mouth!

base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Time ran out! Indecision has consequences — you lost ground on key metrics.

base_rounds.title: Round 2: Pricing Strategy
base_rounds.story: Your product is almost ready. Now comes the crucial question: how much should you charge? Too high and students won't buy. Too low and you won't cover costs. Your cost per unit is ₹80. Sneha is pricing hers at ₹150.
base_rounds.image_prompt: Indian teenager standing at a shop counter weighing price tags on a balance scale, rupee coins and product prototypes on the table, thought bubbles showing different price points, colorful market bazaar backdrop, educational illustration
base_rounds.goal: Set the right price point for maximum impact

choices.label: Premium: ₹200
choices.description: Price high to signal quality. Your product is worth it!
choices.feedback: Premium pricing positions your brand as aspirational! You'll attract fewer but higher-value customers. This is the strategy luxury brands like Apple use. The risk? Some students might find it too expensive.

choices.label: Competitive: ₹130
choices.description: Price just below Sneha. Competitive but sustainable.
choices.feedback: Smart competitive pricing! You're positioned as the value choice. This 'just below the competitor' strategy is called psychological pricing — it makes customers feel they're getting a better deal.

choices.label: Budget: ₹99
choices.description: Go low to capture maximum market share fast.
choices.feedback: Aggressive penetration pricing! You'll win volume but margins are thin. This is how Jio disrupted the telecom market — low prices to grab market share first, then build loyalty.

base_rounds.title: Round 3: Marketing Campaign
base_rounds.story: The mela is in 5 days! Time to launch your marketing campaign. You've got your brand and price locked in. Now you need to spread the word. Where do you focus your marketing energy?
base_rounds.image_prompt: Indian teenagers creating a vibrant marketing campaign, filming a product video with a smartphone on a tripod, colorful posters and social media mockups spread around them, school corridor decorated with promotional banners, dynamic and creative illustration
base_rounds.goal: Design and launch an effective marketing campaign

choices.label: Instagram & YouTube Blitz
choices.description: Create reels, stories, and a product demo video. Budget: ₹1,000 for promoted posts.
choices.feedback: Digital first! Your reels go mini-viral in school circles. The YouTube demo video builds trust. This is modern marketing — content is king! Indian D2C brands like Mamaearth grew entirely through social media.

choices.label: Campus Ambassador Program
choices.description: Recruit 5 popular students to promote your product. Give them free samples.
choices.feedback: Influencer marketing at the grassroots! Your ambassadors create authentic buzz. Word-of-mouth from trusted peers is the most powerful marketing channel for teens. This is how brands like boAt grew in India!

choices.label: Guerrilla Marketing Stunt
choices.description: Plan a surprise flash demo during lunch break. Memorable but risky!
choices.feedback: Bold move! The flash demo creates massive buzz — everyone's talking about it! Guerrilla marketing is all about creating unexpected, memorable experiences. Red Bull built their brand on stunts like this!

base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Time ran out! Indecision has consequences — you lost ground on key metrics.

base_rounds.title: Round 4: Crisis Management
base_rounds.story: Disaster strikes! A negative review appears on the school's anonymous gossip page claiming your product is 'overrated'. Sneha's fans are amplifying it. Your brand reputation is at stake!
base_rounds.image_prompt: Worried Indian teenager looking at a phone screen showing negative comments, storm clouds gathering over a school building, other students whispering in the background, tense atmosphere with dramatic shadows, moody but colorful illustration
base_rounds.goal: Handle the crisis and protect your brand reputation

choices.label: Respond with Grace
choices.description: Post a thoughtful public response acknowledging the feedback and sharing improvements.
choices.feedback: Class act! Your mature response wins respect. Customers see you as transparent and humble. This is what PR experts call 'owning the narrative'. Brands like Tata are known for graceful crisis responses.

choices.label: Launch a Counter-Campaign
choices.description: Release customer testimonials and a behind-the-scenes video showing quality.
choices.feedback: Fighting back with facts! Customer testimonials are powerful social proof. Your transparency turns skeptics into supporters. This is the 'show, don't tell' approach to reputation management.

choices.label: Ignore and Double Down
choices.description: Don't feed the trolls. Focus all energy on improving the product for mela day.
choices.feedback: Sometimes the best response is no response. You used the energy to improve your product. However, letting negative buzz go unchecked did cost some market share. In the social media age, silence can be risky.

base_rounds.title: Round 5: Mela Day — The Grand Finale!
base_rounds.story: It's finally here — Inter-School Mela day! Your booth is set up, products are displayed, and the gates are about to open. Sneha's booth looks impressive across the hall. You have one last chance to make an impact. How do you play your final card?
base_rounds.image_prompt: Bustling Indian school mela with colorful decorated booths, Indian teenager proudly standing at their product display, crowds of excited students and parents, festive bunting and bright lights, panoramic and celebratory illustration
base_rounds.goal: Maximize your sales and brand impact on mela day

choices.label: Live Product Demo
choices.description: Run live demonstrations every 30 minutes. Let the product sell itself!
choices.feedback: Experiential marketing wins the day! Students who tried your product became instant fans. Live demos convert skeptics to buyers faster than any ad. This is why Apple stores have hands-on product displays!

choices.label: Bundle Deal Offer
choices.description: Create combo packs with special mela pricing. Buy 2, get 1 free!
choices.feedback: Bundles drive volume! The 'Buy 2 Get 1 Free' offer creates urgency and increases average order value. This is a classic retail strategy used by everyone from Amazon to your local kirana store!

choices.label: Collaboration Booth
choices.description: Partner with another club's booth (food + your product) for cross-promotion.
choices.feedback: Collaboration over competition! Your cross-promotion brings both booths more foot traffic. This is co-marketing — the same strategy Uber and Spotify used together. Smart partnerships multiply your reach!

base_rounds.timeout_feedback: Time ran out! Indecision has consequences — you lost ground on key metrics.

how_to_play: Watch the story intro and make choices that shape your starting advantage
Each round presents a marketing challenge — choose your strategy wisely
Chat with Professor Priya for marketing advice or Arjun for customer feedback
Keep an eye on Sneha — she'll react to your moves and taunt you!
Balance your budget, brand awareness, and customer satisfaction
AI generates unique challenges based on your play style
Aim for the highest market share by the end of the game

crisis_events.title: Negative Product Feedback!
crisis_events.description: You receive a flood of negative reviews about your product from a popular online forum. Students are criticizing its usability and design, and your brand awareness may take a hit if you don't act fast.

choices.label: Address the feedback
choices.description: Allocate budget to enhance product design based on the feedback received.
choices.feedback: By addressing the concerns, you improve customer satisfaction, but your budget takes a hit.

choices.label: Ignore the feedback
choices.description: Decide to stick with your current product and hope the reviews fade away.
choices.feedback: Ignoring the feedback results in a temporary dip in brand awareness as customers lose trust.

crisis_events.title: Competitor Launches Aggressive Campaign!
crisis_events.description: Your main competitor, Sneha Kapoor, launches a massive marketing campaign that threatens to overshadow your brand. You need quick action to counter their efforts.

choices.label: Boost your advertising
choices.description: Invest additional budget into an advertising blitz to regain visibility.
choices.feedback: The aggressive advertising helps you reclaim some market share, but your budget is significantly reduced.

choices.label: Launch a limited-time promotion
choices.description: Offer a special promotion to attract customers and steal some of Sneha's thunder.
choices.feedback: The promotion increases customer satisfaction and awareness, but at the expense of long-term brand image.

crisis_events.title: Supply Chain Disruption!
crisis_events.description: A sudden supply chain disruption has affected your ability to deliver products on time. Customers are getting restless, and your reputation is on the line.

choices.label: Rush an order
choices.description: Spend extra funds to expedite shipping and fulfill orders quickly.
choices.feedback: Rushing the order boosts customer satisfaction significantly, but you take a hit to your budget.

choices.label: Communicate the delay
choices.description: Inform customers about the delay and offer them a discount for their patience.
choices.feedback: While being transparent costs some customer satisfaction, it maintains brand awareness and trust.

interdependencies.message: When the budget is low, there are fewer resources available for creative development, which limits innovative marketing ideas.
High brand awareness leads to increased visibility and recognition, which attracts more customers and ultimately increases market share.
Low customer satisfaction can lead to negative word-of-mouth and decreased sales, thereby reducing the available budget for future investments.

news_events.headline: India's youth are increasingly turning to entrepreneurship, sparking a wave of innovation across the country.
Market experts advise on the importance of brand identity in capturing the attention of young consumers.
Marketing campaigns are driving student engagement, with digital platforms leading the charge.
Mela Day showcases the best of Indian startups, celebrating creativity and innovation among young entrepreneurs.

dynamic_news_rules.headline: Your exceptional budgeting has led to increased brand visibility, attracting significant attention from investors.
Recent surveys reveal a troubling decline in customer satisfaction, prompting urgent calls for improvement.
Your brand is becoming a household name among Indian students, thanks to effective marketing strategies.

endings.title: Marketing Maestro
endings.description: You've transformed your innovative idea into a beloved brand that resonates with young minds across India! With exceptional brand awareness and customer satisfaction, you've set a benchmark in the marketing world, inspiring future entrepreneurs to dream big.

endings.title: Strategic Success
endings.description: Your clever pricing and effective marketing campaign have won the hearts of your audience! You've established a solid presence in the market, showing that with creativity and smart choices, success is within reach.

endings.title: Decent Effort
endings.description: You managed to make an impact with your brand, gaining valuable insights along the way. Although there's room for improvement, your journey has taught you essential lessons about marketing and business strategies that will help you in the future.

endings.title: Learning Journey
endings.description: Every great marketer starts somewhere, and your journey has been filled with valuable experiences. While the outcome may not be what you hoped for, you have gained insights and skills that will serve you well in your future endeavors.

glossary_terms.definition: Best Alternative To a Negotiated Agreement — your fallback if no deal is reached.
glossary_terms.example: If you can't agree on a price, you could sell to a different buyer — that's your BATNA.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: A strong BATNA gives negotiating power. Knowing both parties' BATNAs reveals who needs the deal more.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: A job applicant with another offer has a stronger BATNA and can negotiate more confidently.

glossary_terms.definition: Finding solutions where both parties gain value rather than one side winning at the other's expense.
glossary_terms.example: Agreeing on a payment plan that works for both buyer and seller, rather than a discount that hurts profit.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Integrative negotiation expands the 'pie' by identifying trade-offs where each party values things differently.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Labor-management negotiations that increase productivity in exchange for better wages can benefit both sides.

glossary_terms.definition: Setting an initial reference point in a negotiation that influences the final outcome.
glossary_terms.example: The first price mentioned in a negotiation becomes the anchor around which all counteroffers are compared.
glossary_terms.deep_dive: Research shows people are heavily influenced by the first number they hear, even when irrelevant.
glossary_terms.real_world_example: Salary negotiations: starting with a high number tends to result in higher final offers.

coaching_moment: Understand core marketing concepts (4Ps, segmentation, positioning). Learn to allocate budgets strategically across marketing channels.
cultural_context: India's marketing landscape is uniquely complex — 22 official languages, diverse regional cultures, and a digital divide between urban and rural consumers. This game develops the creative and strategic thinking that India's marketing professionals must master.
reflection_prompt: How did you adapt as the AI shifted strategies? Which adaptation worked best?
